title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 5 Primo: salvos fieri vs facere — preceptive will, not decretive
pass_a_gloss: But if this opinion does not please, what then is the sense of the Apostle's words? First, it must be noticed that the Apostle did not say, God wills to make all men saved, and to draw them to the knowledge of the truth by the efficacy of preaching and of the Spirit; but, he wills all to be saved, and to come to the knowledge of the truth. For to God willing to make someone saved no human will resists, as Augustine truly says in De correptione et gratia chapter 14. By these words therefore is expressed rather what God wills to be done by men, than what he wills to do in men. God wills that Gospel ministers be bound, as far as in them lies, to strive that all may be saved and come to Christ; he wills that individual Christians by praying, and by other means they can, promote the salvation of all men. It is ours, says Augustine, who do not know who belongs to the number of the predestined, to will that all be saved, chapter 15. These words therefore pertain to the preceptive will, which directs men; not to the decretive will, which infallibly bestows the good destined for a man.
pass_b_english: If that reading fails, what do Paul's words mean? First notice: he did not say God wills to make all men saved and drag them to the truth by the force of preaching and the Spirit. He said he wills all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Timothy 2:4). When God wills to make someone saved, no human will blocks him — so Augustine, On Rebuke and Grace 14. These words show what God wills people to do, more than what he wills to work inside them. He wills gospel ministers, as far as they can, to labor that all may be saved and come to Christ; he wills each Christian, by prayer and every means he can, to further the salvation of all. It is ours, Augustine says, who do not know who belongs to the number of the predestined, to will that all be saved (On Rebuke and Grace 15). So the text belongs to the preceptive will that directs us — not to the decretive will that infallibly gives the good God has destined for a person.
source_text: Verum si non placet haec sententia, quis tandem sensus verborum Apostoli? Primo, animadvertendum est, non dixisse Apostolum, Deus vult omnes homines salvos facere, & ad agnitionem veritatis efficacia praedicationis & Spiritus pertrahere; sed, vult omnes salvos fieri, & venire ad cognitionem veritatis. Nam Deo volenti salvum facere nullum hominum resistit arbitrium, ut vere Augustinus De corrept. & grat. cap. 14. Hisce igitur verbis exprimitur potius quid Deus velit ab hominibus fieri, quam quid velit in hominibus facere. Vult Deus, ut Ministri Evangelici teneantur, quantum in illis est, niti ut omnes salvi fiant, & ad Christum veniant; vult ut singuli Christiani orando, aliisque quibus possunt modis, promoveant salutem omnium hominum. Nostrum est, inquit Augustinus, qui nescimus quisnam pertineat ad numerum praedestinatorum, velle omnes salvos fieri, cap. 15. Ad voluntatem igitur praecipientem, quae homines dirigit, haec verba pertinent; non ad voluntatem decernentem, quae bonum homini destinatum infallibiliter largitur.
